title: 3.7.18 Lab: Build a New Object with Spread + Override
description: Use object spread to copy an object with one property overridden and one property added, leaving the original untouched. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the base object
steps.instructions: The starter gives you settings, an object with three properties: const settings = { theme: "dark", fontSize: 14, wrap: true }; Leave that line as it is.

steps.title: Copy with one property overridden
steps.instructions: Use object spread to build a copy of settings called changed, with one existing property changed. The override must be written after the spread.

steps.title: Copy with a new property added
steps.instructions: Use object spread again to build a second copy called extended, with a new property that settings did not have.

steps.title: Log all three objects
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print both copies and the original settings object. Confirm the original is unchanged.

requirements.title: Object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Declare an object in braces with at least three name: value pairs.

requirements.title: Object spread used
requirements.description: Uses object spread, written as ... inside an object literal. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Spread is three dots in front of an object, written inside the braces of a new object.

requirements.title: Override after the spread
requirements.description: Writes a property after the spread so the override wins. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Write the property you want to change AFTER the spread. The later entry wins.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: settings is unchanged and both copies differ from it in the right way
requirements.description: After the code runs, settings is still { theme: "dark", fontSize: 14, wrap: true } and at least three lines were printed. Help: 3.7.15 (Example: Spread Override)
requirements.hint: Build each copy with object spread ({ ...settings, fontSize: 18 }) and print all three. Never assign into settings itself.

checks.expr: Object.keys(changed).length === 3 && Object.keys(changed).filter(k => changed[k] !== settings[k]).length === 1 && Object.keys(extended).length === 4 && Object.keys(settings).every(k => extended[k] === settings[k]) && (J => Object.values(changed).every(v => J.includes(String(v))) && Object.values(extended).every(v => J.includes(String(v))))(output.join(' ')) && !same('changed', 'settings') && !same('extended', 'settings')
checks.fail: changed should be settings with exactly one property changed, extended should be settings plus one new property, settings itself must stay the same, and your output should show both copies.
